 Judgment

Since these two appeals arise from the very same award dated 30.10.2013 in O.P.(MV) No.411 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Wayanad, Kalpetta, these appeals are heard together and being disposed of by this judgment.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Wayanad, Kalpetta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.A.C.A.No.1722 of 2014 is filed by the 3 rd respondent insurer, challenging quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, whereas M.A.C.A No.437 of 2015 is filed by the 2 nd respondent/previous owner of the vehicle in the O.P challenging the finding of the tribunal granting the insurer the recovery right to recover the compensation amount from the appellant herein, who was the previous owner of the vehicle.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. Brief facts of the case is as follows :-
On 04.01.2007 at about 02.00 pm, while the petitioner was travelling on a motorcycle, an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KL-10-M-6742 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner came from a pocket road, hit against the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, he sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 2,00,000/-.
Respondents 1, 2, 3 and 5 are the driver, previous owner, insurer and RC owner of the offending vehicle respectively.
The 3rd respondent filed a written statement disputing the liability and also the driving licence of the driver.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A7 and Exts.B1 and B2 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 94,043/- as compensation under different heads with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the 3rd respondent, insurer and granted right of recovery to the 3rd respondent from the 2nd respondent-owner.
4.
Heard the learned counsel for the claimant, the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent/previous owner and the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant insurance company.
Though notice was served on the 5th respondent, he chose not to appear before this Court.

5. The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the tribunal had originally passed the award on 29.10.2011 awarding a total amount of 77,340/- with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment against the 3rd respondent with right of recovery from the 2nd respondent .

Thereafter, the 2 nd respondent, who is the previous owner MACA NOs. 1722 OF 2014 & 437 OF 2015 2025:KER:49992 of the vehicle filed a petition to set aside the ex parte award before the tribunal and the tribunal thereafter set aside the original award passed on 29.10.2011 and passed a modified award on 30.10.2013 awarding an enhancement amount of 94,043/- as compensation under different heads with interest @7.5% per annum from Sharafudheen vs Shanoj K.M. , S/O.Mani on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145875201/
3 the date of petition till realization with proportionate cost and recover from the 2 nd respondent.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal ought not to have granted enhancement of compensation, as the issue regarding compensation had already been decided in the earlier award.
Since the claimant did not file any appeal or petition challenging the said award, the amount granted therein ought to have remained unchanged.

I find no merit in the contention advanced by the learned standing counsel, for the reason that the original award was set aside on an application filed by the 2nd respondent, who was the previous owner of the vehicle.
Once the award was set aside, there remained no award dated 29.10.2011.

However, upon setting aside the original award and passing a modified award, the Tribunal found it just and proper to enhance the compensation when compared to what was granted under the earlier award.
Therefore, I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Accordingly, the modified award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, and the insurance company is not entitled to succeed MACA NOs. 1722 OF 2014 & 437 OF 2015 2025:KER:49992 on that ground.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent/previous owner in MACA No.437 of 2015 submits that before the tribunal as well as in the written statement filed by the 2 nd respondent, he has specifically contended that the vehicle was transferred to 4 th respondent and subsequent to the 5th respondent on 11.09.2006.

Since the accident occurred on 04.01.2007, the 5 th respondent was the registered owner as on the date of accident and he was liable to pay the amount awarded by the tribunal and not the appellant herein.
It is further submitted that in the written statement filed by additional 5 th respondent also it was admitted that he was the registered owner of the vehicle at the time of accident.

However, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that, since the policy stood in the name of the 2 nd respondent, he cannot be exonerated from the liability to pay the award passed by the tribunal.

7. On a perusal of the award, it is seen that in the written statement filed by the 5th respondent, he has specifically admitted that he was the registered owner of the autorickshaw as on the date of the accident, i.e., 04.01.2007.
The insurance company in paragraph 10 of the award has also found that the 5 th respondent admitted his ownership of the vehicle and only disputed the liability.

Though it was MACA NOs. 1722 OF 2014 & 437 OF 2015 2025:KER:49992 found that the 5th respondent was the registered owner of the vehicle, the Tribunal held that there was no privity of contract between the insurer and the registered owner, as the policy stood in the name of the previous owner, namely the 2nd respondent in the O.P.
8.

In Naveen Kumar v. Vijay Kumar [(2018) 3 SCC 1], a three- Judge Bench of this Court held that in view of the definition of the expression 'owner' in Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered, who, for the purposes of the said Act,
would be treated as the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar v. Vijay Kumar [(2018) 3 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the registered owner purports to transfer the vehicle, but continues to be reflected in the records of the Registering Authority as the owner of the vehicle, he would not stand absolved of his liability as owner.

Therefore, even though the insurance policy had not been transferred to the name of the registered owner, the previous owner could not be held liable though the policy stands in the name of the previous owner.
It is the registered owner who is liable to satisfy the award amount awarded by the tribunal.

Accordingly, I am of the view that the finding of the Tribunal granting the right of recovery from the 2nd respondent is unsustainable Sharafudheen vs Shanoj K.M. , S/O.Mani on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145875201/
4 and is liable to be set aside

In the result, MACA No.1722 of 2014 filed by the insurance company will stand dismissed and MACA No.437 of 2015 filed by the MACA NOs. 1722 OF 2014 & 437 OF 2015 2025:KER:49992 2nd owner/previous owner of the vehicle is allowed.
The order passed by the tribunal granting right of recovery to the insurer to recover the said amount from the 2nd respondent in the Original Petition is hereby set aside.

It is made clear that the insurance company is entitled to recover the award amount passed by the tribunal from the 5 th respondent (Shahul Hameed), who was the registered owner at the time of accident.
